questions.explain: Production database traffic belongs on dedicated circuits (Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, Cloud Interconnect) — consistent latency, no internet traversal, SLA-backed — with redundancy from day one (two circuits or circuit plus VPN failover).
options: Public internet with TLS
Site-to-site VPN for all production database traffic
Dedicated circuits (Direct Connect/ExpressRoute/Cloud Interconnect), designed redundant from day one
Dial-up backup lines
questions.q: What network foundation does Chapter 27 require for hybrid production database traffic?

questions.explain: For the initial multi-terabyte seed, physical media shipment (AWS Snowball, Azure Data Box) beats the network when the math favors it.
options: Physical media shipment (AWS Snowball, Azure Data Box) when the math favors it
Transactional replication of the full history
BCP over the VPN
Re-typing the data into the cloud database
questions.q: How should the initial multi-terabyte seeding of a cloud target be done?

questions.explain: Hybrid DR runs both directions; cloud-to-on-premises is always harder because on-premises capacity is fixed. The critical question is capacity: the DR side must actually absorb the production workload.
options: On-premises to cloud, because the cloud has no elasticity
Cloud to on-premises, because on-premises capacity is fixed and the DR target must actually absorb the workload
Both directions are equally easy
Only the on-premises-to-cloud direction needs designing
questions.q: Which hybrid DR direction is harder, and why?

questions.explain: For SQL Server estates this almost always means AD/Entra ID spanning both worlds — and the failure mode is authentication that works inside each world but breaks across the boundary, so cross-boundary authentication must be tested explicitly and continuously with a scheduled probe.
options: Separate domains with no trust, for isolation
Local SQL logins only
One identity system (AD/Entra ID) across both worlds, with a scheduled probe that authenticates to every SQL Server from every network segment
Email-based password resets
questions.q: What is the hybrid identity pattern and its key operational discipline?

questions.explain: Never run chatty cross-boundary queries — a linked-server query pulling a million rows row-by-row across the link is the classic hybrid performance disaster. Rewrite as a single bulk operation, keep joins local, and replicate slow-changing dimensions on a schedule.
options: Use cursors to fetch rows one at a time
Increase the linked-server timeout
Never run chatty cross-boundary queries — rewrite as bulk operations, keep joins local, cache reference data
Always join across the boundary for accuracy
questions.q: What is the performance rule for queries spanning the hybrid boundary?
